subject: Swift 6.4.0-RELEASE (open-source toolchain, Linux static musl SDK) miscompiles an inout uniqueness check in a generic class's tail walk; NTSDCore OriginalRetainedHistory fixed without changing behaviour

symptom.x86_64: every NTSDHeadless scenario exited 139 (SIGSEGV) right after the 'started' event (docker --platform linux/amd64 under Rosetta); reproduced identically under QEMU 10.0.13 user mode (debian:trixie), so not a Rosetta artefact (QEMU 8.2.2 from ubuntu:24.04 crashes internally even without arguments and was not used)
symptom.backtrace: qemu-x86_64 -g + gdb-multiarch: swift_isUniquelyReferenced_nonNull_native (rdi=0, mov 0x8(%rdi)) <- isKnownUniquelyReferenced<T> (ManagedBuffer.swift:708) <- OriginalRetainedHistory.Node.deinit (OriginalRetainedHistory.swift:15) <- OriginalApplicationIterationDelivery destroy <- OriginalApplicationPreparedStartupPlatform deinit <- OriginalApplicationHostSession.step

codegen.linux-x86_64 (swift-6.4.0-RELEASE, -O): lea -0x38(%rbp),%r15; mov %r15,%rdi; call $ss25isKnownUniquelyReferencedySbxzRlzClF -- the node (r14) is never stored to -0x38(%rbp)
codegen.linux-aarch64 (swift-6.4.0-RELEASE, -O): add x0, sp, #0x8; bl $ss25isKnownUniquelyReferencedySbxzRlzClF -- the node (x21) is never stored to [sp,#8]
codegen.macOS arm64 (Xcode Swift 6.4, swiftlang-: str x22, [sp, #0x8] before the call and ldr x0, [sp, #0x8] after: correct; the shipping AppKit app is unaffected
codegen.Optional-overload rewrite on Linux: also no store, and the call is hoisted out of the loop (checked once)
codegen.mechanism: inference: the optimizer treats the unspecialised generic isKnownUniquelyReferenced call as not reading the inout slot (the Linux SDK ships only a binary Swift.swiftmodule, so the attribute was not read directly)

variants.linked: the shipped shape: non-generic link with releaseTail() called from the generic node's deinit

linux-x86_64.fixed: exit 0 but silently truncates shared tails (older kept 1, expected 5; unique-then-shared 1, expected 3)

linux-aarch64.original: truncates a shared tail (1, expected 5) then exit 139 (an earlier build exited 135, SIGBUS)

reproducer.note: results of the miscompiled variants vary between builds/runs (undefined behaviour); silent truncation means the miscompile could corrupt another copy's history, not only crash

fix.change: next and the iterative tail walk move to a private non-generic class OriginalRetainedHistoryLink (final releaseTail()); the generic Node subclasses it and calls releaseTail() from its deinit, so each node's tail is still released before its own element; elements downcasts links with unsafeDowncast (every link is a Node of the same Element)
fix.codegen after: releaseTail calls swift_isUniquelyReferenced_nonNull_native on the loaded reference inside the loop (x86_64 and aarch64 Linux); no generic isKnownUniquelyReferenced call remains in the Node deinit
fix.review: independent read-only reviewer: semantic equivalence OK (walk, stop point, node/element release order, count, elements, value semantics), unsafeDowncast/access OK, no other occurrences; it asked for a unique-then-shared test, added as testDroppingANewerCopyReleasesOnlyItsOwnNodes

gates.macOS: release test build ok; OriginalRetainedHistoryTests 5/5; 699 tests listed; Xcode release build; app_e2e --build --scenario all 9/10 = baseline (playback pre-existing on main)
gates.linux-x86_64 headless (Rosetta harness): 9/10 equal to the frozen AppKit references; playback differs as on main (alert at iteration 251)
gates.linux-aarch64 headless: 9/10 equal to the frozen AppKit references; playback differs as on main
gates.frames: all 63 captured frames byte-identical between x86_64 and aarch64 Linux runs with the fix, and identical to the earlier aarch64 run without it

consequence: the earlier aarch64 headless results (crossplatform-headless-vs-20261004.json, crossplatform-headless-scenarios-linux-20261004.jsonl) came from a binary with this undefined behaviour; they are kept unchanged and superseded by the reruns with the fix
open: the Linux XCTest runs (glibc aarch64) of the old code were not rerun in release mode to show the test failing there
reporting the compiler bug upstream needs the user's approval (publication)
